prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals in the Green Party Manifesto 2024 (ideology-neutral)

Health and care
- NHS: Additional revenue funding rising to £28bn/yr by 2030; at least £20bn capital over five years. Reduce waiting lists, rapid GP access, guaranteed NHS dentistry, higher NHS pay, more primary care funding (£1.5bn/yr by 2030), £2bn primary care capital, restore public health budgets (+£1.5bn), expand community diagnostics. Support NHS Reinstatement Bill to end marketisation.
- Dentistry: New NHS contract; funding reaching £3bn/yr by 2030; preventive community hubs; free dental nursing for children/low-income groups.
- Mental health: Access to evidence-based therapies within 28 days; counsellor in every school and sixth-form college; tailored provision for specific groups; better SEND support.
- Drugs policy: National Commission to reform laws; move towards regulated markets; decriminalise personal possession and divert to health support.
- Assisted dying: Support legal change with safeguards.
- HIV: Aim to end new transmissions by 2030; expand opt-out A&E testing.

Social care and disability
- Free personal care; £20bn/yr investment; national career structure and pay for carers; protections for overseas care workers; “Gloria’s Law” for essential Care Supporters.
- Disability: Immediate 5% benefit uplift; oppose PIP voucher plans; reform assessments; free transport for 16–18 SEND pupils; workplace support.
- Children’s social care: +£3bn to councils; guaranteed counselling; extend “staying put” to 21.

Housing and planning
- Build 150,000 social homes/yr; end Right to Buy; bring empty homes into use; rent controls via councils; end Section 21; longer tenancies; tenant right to energy upgrades.
- Standards: New homes to Passivhaus-equivalent with solar and low-carbon heating; raise PRS to EPC C.
- Retrofit: £29bn for home insulation (five years), £4bn for public buildings, £9bn for low-carbon heating, £7bn for heat-adaptation; area-based delivery and property-linked finance.
- Planning: Stronger local authority role; whole-life carbon in applications; reuse of materials; reduce car-dependency in new developments.

Energy and climate
- No new oil/gas licences; end subsidies; carbon tax starting £120/t rising to £500/t within 10 years.
- Electricity: Target c.70% from wind by 2030; end de facto ban on onshore wind; 80GW offshore, 53GW onshore, 100GW solar by 2035; support marine/hydro/geothermal; rooftop solar on new homes.
- Grid/storage: Expand grid, interconnectors, offshore networks; scale energy storage; green hydrogen for industry.
- Community energy: Minimum community ownership thresholds; remove barriers; regional bank investment.
- Nuclear: Stop new build; phase out existing plants.

Economy, tax and ownership
- Green investment averaging £40bn/yr (energy, retrofit, rail, public transport, active travel, industry, water/sewage).
- Public ownership: Rail, water companies, and Big 5 retail energy suppliers.
- Tax: Wealth tax 1% >£10m, 2% >£1bn; align CGT and investment income with earnings; remove NIC upper limit; reform inheritance tax; council tax revaluation; move toward Land Value Tax; windfall taxes on oil/gas and banks; VAT changes (cut for hospitality/arts, raise on financial services/private education); carbon tax as above; anti-avoidance measures. Borrow to invest within inflation constraints.

Work and welfare
- Repeal anti-union laws; Charter of Workers’ Rights; day-one rights; £15 minimum wage (support for small firms); 10:1 pay ratio cap; gig workers classed as “workers”; equal pay audits; support shorter working hours.
- Benefits: +£40/week to UC and legacy benefits; end five-week wait; abolish two-child cap and bedroom tax; carers’ allowance +10%; pensions uprated with inflation and wages; end sanctions; long-term aim for Universal Basic Income.

Nature, animals, food
- Rights of Nature Act; 30% land/sea protected by 2030; Clean Air Act; Right to Roam; +£1.5bn DEFRA; public ownership of water; £3bn/yr grants for nature recovery; peatland rewetting; ban destructive fishing in MPAs.
- Animal welfare: Commission on Animal Protection; ban blood sports; end factory farming practices incl. cages; phase out animal testing; ban lead ammo; end badger cull.
- Food/farming: Nearly triple farm support; link payments to reduced pesticides; expand horticulture; free school meals for all and primary breakfast clubs; food education; strengthen Grocery Code; boost domestic production and local food networks; expand productive forestry and wood reuse.

Education
- Schools: +£8bn (incl. £2bn for teacher pay); £2.5bn/yr for safe buildings/RAAC; broaden curriculum; abolish Ofsted; SEND investment £5bn; counsellors and school nurses.
- Early years: £1.4bn/yr for Sure Start; 35 hours childcare from 9 months (sector negotiation).
- FE/HE: +£3bn for sixth form; £12bn for FE/skills; restore EMA; scrap tuition fees; restore maintenance grants; address TPS impacts; move academies/free schools to LA control; VAT on private school fees; keep RSE incl. LGBTIQA+ content.

Transport
- Raise rail/bus subsidy to £10bn/yr by end of parliament; £19bn over five years for public transport, electrification, cycling/walking; public ownership of rail; local control of buses; free bus travel for under-18s; £2.5bn/yr for active travel.
- Roads: Oppose new roads; restore fuel duty escalator; road pricing; end new ICE car sales by 2027; end ICE use by 2035; weight-based VED; 20mph default in built-up areas; EV scrappage up to £5bn/yr; rapid charging rollout.
- Aviation: Frequent-flyer levy; ban domestic flights where rail <3 hours; tax kerosene via carbon tax; halt airport expansion; reskilling for workers.

Democracy, rights, migration, culture
- Elections/democracy: Repeal voter ID; proportional representation; replace House of Lords with elected chamber; votes at 16; tighter lobbying/media transparency; fair party funding; expand devolution and local government funding (+£5bn/yr).
- Rights: Defend HRA/ECHR; restore legal aid; scrap recent protest-curbing laws; support trans self-ID; X marker on passports; scrap Prevent.
- Migration/asylum: End “hostile environment”; safe routes; right to work while claims processed; abolish NRPF and 10-year route; limit detention; create Department of Migration; fees at cost; NHS access; remove spousal income thresholds; family reunification.
- Culture/media/digital: £5bn over five years for local arts/sport; protect venues/night-time economy; VAT exemption for cultural events; media ownership caps (max 20% market share); implement Leveson; Digital Bill of Rights; precautionary AI regulation; protect creators’ IP; EU touring visas for artists.

Justice and policing
- End routine stop-and-search and facial recognition; strengthen accountability; expand restorative justice; presumption against custodial sentences <2 years; invest £11bn over parliament to restore MoJ, legal aid, courts; make misogyny a hate crime; fund VAWG services; decriminalise sex work; fund youth services; safeguards on police interactions with young people.

Foreign policy
- Support Ukraine; seek EU re-entry (steps: customs union, free movement, Erasmus); increase aid to 1% GNI and climate finance to 1.5% GNI by 2033, including Loss and Damage Fund; back ecocide law and debt relief; end ISDS-type trade courts.
- Israel/Palestine: Immediate bilateral ceasefire; recognise Palestine; end UK arms exports to Israel; pursue war-crimes accountability.
- Nuclear/NATO: Sign TPNW, cancel Trident; work within NATO for “no first use” and stronger focus on diplomacy.
